oneLiner: Correct, deterministic, zero-dependency — and it spends 2,061 context tokens to print a 4-character string.
summary: We fetched SKILL.md v1.0.7 and verified the documented Swatch formula (BMT = UTC+1 fixed, no DST, one beat = 86.4s) with two independent reimplementations instead of executing the bundled script. Both returned @058 at 2026-08-08T00:24:34Z — the math is right, rollover is handled (%1000, @000 at day end), and it takes ISO timestamps for timezone conversion. It needs nothing but python3: no network, no credentials, no privileges. The catch is proportion: the SKILL.md costs ~2,061 tokens of your agent's context before a single beat is printed. Great citizen, expensive tenant.

evidence.output: 1 flag — output-directive: "Output ONLY the beat time… no reasoning, no explanation". Benign formatting demand, but it is an instruction aimed at your agent; no override attempts, no network calls, no shell risk, required_privileges: none.

evidence.label: Independent verification of the documented formula (script not executed)
evidence.run: python3: beat = int(((UTC+1h) seconds of day) / 86.4) % 1000  — cross-checked with day-fraction method
evidence.output: UTC 2026-08-08T00:24:34Z → BMT seconds 5074 → @058 (method 1) — @058 (method 2). Matches the skill's documented algorithm exactly.

evidence.label: Agent-fit checks
evidence.run: headless / parseable / determinism review of SKILL.md
evidence.output: Headless: yes (pure python3, no prompts). Deterministic for a given second. Output contract is strict and zero-padded (@000–@999) — trivially parseable. Edge case documented: beat 1000 renders as @000.

goodFor: A harmless first skill to test an install pipeline end-to-end
Agents that answer '/beats' or Swatch-time trivia
Timezone-free timestamps in logs or dashboards, if you're feeling 1998
notFor: Anything where 2k tokens of context matters more than novelty
Precision timing — it floors to whole beats (86.4s resolution)
